rationale: Submits the tick-period sweep that the placeholder-shift question's discriminator asks for. The retained evidence for the shift sits only at a 1000 ms tick period (the fixed experiment and its repeat), while the observation that the same scenario returned the correct index at 80 ms was construction feedback, so the condition that the queued placeholders must survive the flush-to-truncation window was not receipt-backed at more than one tick period. The harness is parameterised on the tick period: the case becomes `run_shift_case(mode, tick_ms)` with every sleep scaled from it, and three sweep points (100, 250 and 500 ms) join the existing 1000 ms reference as separate cases with their own admissions, result event names and comparisons. Locally the 500 ms point already shifts - `resolved` = ok with `assigned_idx` 3 while entry 33 is at index 1 and the decided log is 33,34,35 - so that point at least is expected to be violated, and the two lower points are the ones that would narrow the condition if they return the correct index. This is a revision of the fixed experiment because the harness bytes and the case set changed; its previous revision and both of its receipts stay in the record.

investigations.discriminator: Pending: the sweep's receipt. A correct index at 100 or 250 ms would show the shift needs a tick period well above the gap and would narrow the condition; violations there would show the window is wider than the retained single-point evidence suggests. Locally, 500 ms violates; 80 ms was construction feedback only.

experiment.revision_reason: Tick-period sweep: the single case is parameterised into `run_shift_case(mode, tick_ms)` (all sleeps derived from the tick period) and three sweep points are added as separate cases - 100 ms, 250 ms and 500 ms - each emitting its own admission and result event, with comparisons declared against the same obligation. The scenario, the batch size (3), the election and resend tick counts, and the 1000 ms reference case are unchanged; a fresh execution is required because the harness bytes and the case set changed.

scope.description: Three runs of the same lost-entry scenario at different tick periods (100, 250 and 500 ms). Each run buffers two `append_notify` entries in the leader's batch of three, cuts the leader off from both followers so they take over and decide entry 22, restores the links so the leader flushes its batch and is truncated back to the new leader's log, re-elects it, and then buffers a fresh `append_notify` (entry 33) together with two filler appends (34, 35). Every run reports the fresh call's resolution, the index it returns, the true position of entry 33 in the decided log, whether they agree, and the entry at the returned index.
assumptions: The scenario's own sleeps are derived from the tick period so that the phase timings keep the same relation to the tick at each sweep point.
Message loss and the following re-synchronisation are permitted faults; nothing in the harness modifies target logic.
Batching (batch_size 3) is what defers the writes into `unconfirmed_local`, and the batch flushes only when full or on a `Prepare`.
A tick period below the flush-to-truncation gap cannot be sampled here, because the gap itself is not under the harness's control; the sweep brackets the condition from above.
excluded: Any claim about the exact threshold between 250 and 500 ms, or about tick periods below 100 ms.
Any claim about other batch sizes, follower origins, or the arm-order mechanism that the same question already covers.
Any claim about the internal placeholder queue, which is not observable through the public API.

experiment.prefix: For each sweep point: build three actors with batch_size 3 and the case's tick period, node 1 carrying leader_priority 1. Call `try_become_leader()` on node 1 until nodes 1, 2 and 3 all report it as the accepted leader, then emit the admission event. Issue `append_notify(TestEntry(11))` and `append_notify(TestEntry(12))` on node 1 from spawned tasks so both are deferred into its batch. Block node 1's links to nodes 2 and 3 in both directions, wait until nodes 2 and 3 report a leader other than 1, and call `append_notify(TestEntry(22))` on that leader. Unblock the links and sleep several tick periods so node 1 processes the `Prepare` that flushes its batch and the following `AcceptSync` that truncates it back. Then call `try_become_leader()` on node 1 until it reports itself as the accepted leader, spawn `append_notify(TestEntry(33))` on it, follow with two plain appends (34, 35), sleep several ticks, and await the fresh call. Finally read node 1's decided suffix, find the 1-based position of entry 33, read the entry at the returned index, and emit the mode-specific outcome event with those values.
experiment.responsibility: The decisive inputs come from the target: batching defers the writes into `unconfirmed_local`, the re-synchronisation truncates the entries they refer to, and `reconcile_unconfirmed` maps queued placeholders to index advances to compute what it reports to the caller. The harness chooses the schedule (tick period) and reads the endpoints.

comparisons.description: 100 ms tick: if the call resolves Ok, the returned index must be the entry's true position.
500 ms tick: locally this already violated (returned 3 while the entry sits at 1), so a violation is expected.

semantic_changes: Three cases added at 100, 250 and 500 ms ticks; each has its own admission and result event name, and the comparisons assert the same obligation at each point.
